clue.text: Insect biting a skin

indicators.note: something biting holds a piece between its jaws, so the insect word closes round the other piece

parts.note: a fly is a common insect

explanation.surface: A bug sinks its teeth into somebody's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to strip the hide off, so skin as a verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pamper — feed, then provide a free berth inside

indicators.note: the second part of the clue sits inside the word feed, which wraps it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of berth are set free to take a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on spoiling a guest: give them food and then a free bed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' is the anagram signal for BERTH; 'then provide' is linking padding, and the cosy sense of a feather bed lends the definition its flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To featherbed someone is to cosset them with excessive comfort or favour, an idiom for pampering.

clue.text: Outrage when a chum embraces president

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first pieces wrap their arms round the abbreviation

parts.note: a pal is a chum, a friend

explanation.surface: Indignation as a friend is seen hugging the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify, which is what outrage means as a verb.

clue.text: 'Tec in sci-fi drama using what's proven

indicators.note: a drama is a play, so the letters are played about with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the short form of detective
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective turns up in a science-fiction play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drama' is the anagram signal for 'Tec in sci-fi.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientific method relies on tested evidence and established results, the sense of working with demonstrated facts.

clue.text: Game a pain in the neck, English first team concludes

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

indicators.note: the first of the word team means only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A sporting moan: the game is a nuisance, and England's top side finishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concludes' just says the first letter of team ends the answer. CRICKET is the bat-and-ball game played in summer in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket is a sport, and a sport is a kind of game.

clue.text: Spike aircraftman and he is in pain

parts.note: an ear is the spike of a cereal plant such as corn
AC is the RAF abbreviation for aircraftman, the lowest rank
taken as written

explanation.surface: An RAF airman gets spiked and is in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: An aircraftman is the lowest rank in Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: An earache is a particular kind of ache, a specific example of physical pain.

clue.text: Barrel is required for n African port

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cask is needed for shipping goods to a North African harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis, capital of Tunisia, is a harbour city on the North African coast.

clue.text: Cunningly raise fare without any restriction

indicators.note: done cunningly, by a trick, so the letters are shuffled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sly operator puts up ticket prices without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' is the anagram signal for RAISE FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely unconstrained, as unrestricted as the open sky.

clue.text: To be snug, woolly socks need to be partly pulled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, pulled up means the run is read from bottom to top
only part of the words woolly socks is used, a run straddling the two

explanation.surface: To keep warm, pull your woolly socks up a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' picks YSOC from woollY SOCks, and 'pulled up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and snug are synonyms for warm and comfortable.

clue.text: Side track to extended area of land, down under?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, the realm down below, not Australia as the surface hints
a tract is a large expanse of land

explanation.surface: A diversion leads to a vast stretch of Australian outback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' looks like Australia; here it is the underworld, DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack someone is to divert their attention, which is what distract means.

clue.text: It intensifies spread of fire from lamp I overturned

indicators.note: knocked over and upset, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: fire that spreads moves about, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blaze grows after an oil lamp gets knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' makes AMPL from LAMP, I stays as it is, and 'spread' makes FIER from FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An amplifier is a device that boosts a sound or signal, making it stronger.

clue.text: Wants to be noticed returning about five hundred

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word goes round the numeral
returning means the word for noticed is read backwards

parts.note: seen means noticed or spotted
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be spotted coming back with about five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SEEN into NEES; 'about' puts it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs and wants are both nouns or verbs for requirements or desires.

clue.text: Abandoning sloth, becomes a composer

indicators.note: acting with abandon, wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A lazy person gives up idleness and takes up music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning' is the anagram signal for SLOTH; Gustav Holst wrote The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English composer, best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: Trifle making Rex sick, unfortunately, fruit's provided

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated K as on chess pieces

indicators.note: an unlucky outcome upsets things, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the haw is the red fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: Some dessert has made Rex ill; luckily there's fruit as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex usually gives R, but here it means king, K. 'unfortunately' turns SICK into ICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickshaw is a trinket or fancy delicacy, a trifle in the sense of something of little worth.

clue.text: Bullock on plain — give it a wide berth!

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bullock
plain and clear both mean obvious

explanation.surface: Warning about a bull on open grassland: keep well away.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to avoid something by keeping a safe distance.

clue.text: Drive into a section of the defencework

parts.note: to ram is to drive forcefully into something
a part is a section

explanation.surface: An attacker smashes into part of the fortifications.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive earth bank or wall round a fort.

clue.text: Boggy terrain making it hard to touch down on planet

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed below, so hard and touch down go under the planet

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to land is to touch down

explanation.surface: A space probe finds it difficult to set down on another world's swampy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshland is wet, soft ground, which is what boggy terrain describes.

clue.text: Prove to be good at spelling

definitions.text: Prove to be good at spelling

parts.words: Prove to be good at spelling
parts.note: reads like being a good speller, but spelling here means casting spells, as a witch does

explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to cast a spell over, or to charm and delight.

clue.text: Plan of action designed to get Conservative PM again?

indicators.note: designed means made up or arranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A party drive meant to put a Tory leader back in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' is the anagram signal for PM AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised course of action aimed at a goal, such as an election.

clue.text: Unreliable man going about desert

indicators.note: going about means going round, so the man's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Eric is a man's name
to rat is to desert or betray

explanation.surface: Someone unpredictable wanders around a wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable and inconsistent, the sense of not dependable.

clue.text: Once, under wingate's command, scrambled in ditch?

indicators.note: scrambling mixes things up, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier long ago, under his commander, scrambles into a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' is the anagram signal for IN DITCH. Orde Wingate led the Chindits, a British jungle force in Burma in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Chindits were the WWII long-range jungle troops commanded by Orde Wingate, so a past member served under him.

clue.text: Guilt about the little bit left off

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter goes out of the word for a scrap

parts.note: a morsel is a little bit of food

explanation.surface: Someone feels bad about the scrap that was abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L from MORSEL, leaving MORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong done, the feeling of culpability.

clue.text: A soldier to pull back behind the lines?

indicators.note: in a military sense the lines enclose the rear area, so the reversed piece is placed within the word for behind

parts.note: rear means behind, the back part

indicators.note: back means the word for pull is read backwards

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to retreat behind the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal for pull. In military language the rear lies behind the front lines, which is why 'the lines' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier of a standing army, as opposed to a reservist.

clue.text: Of a mind to spare the monarch

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A courtier is inclined to let the king off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' looks like a verb meaning let off, but here it is the adjective meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of a mind to do something means intending or considering it, as in thinking of doing it.

clue.text: Drain repair? You can't sink lower!

indicators.note: a repair sets things in order again, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Fixing a drain: you can't get any lower than that!
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair' is the anagram signal for DRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the bottom from which no further fall is possible.

clue.text: It sounds like the beginning of dictation

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
the start of the word dictation, its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Something resembling the opening of a dictation exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' looks like a hint at what is heard, but ASDIC is the old name for sonar, which sounds the sea by echo.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic is early submarine-detecting sonar, which takes soundings by sending out pulses.

clue.text: Fabric dug up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mined means dug, as from a mine

explanation.surface: Some cloth has been excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill cloth, the stuff of jeans.

clue.text: Refuse to be seen on top

explanation.definitionFit: Scum is worthless refuse or rubbish, and also the froth that forms on the surface of a liquid.

clue.text: Cold, tough vegetable

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hard means tough

explanation.surface: A chilled, chewy green is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green plant eaten as greens, related to beet.

clue.text: Application called for by coach

explanation.definitionFit: Diligence means steady effort, and a diligence was also a public stagecoach in France.

clue.text: In church, ministers roared most terribly

indicators.note: done terribly, very badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Clergy bellowed dreadfully during the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' is the anagram signal for ROARED MOST. In the Church of Scotland the minister chairing an assembly is the Moderator.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches the minister presiding over a church court is called a moderator.

clue.text: Frosty reception when this VIP returns

indicators.note: returns means the word for frost is read backwards

parts.note: rime is a coating of frost, which is what greets a frosty welcome

explanation.surface: A cold welcome awaits when the dignitary comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RIME round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, a very important person.
